title: docs(plugin-security): cite the provenance skip by symbol, not by rotted line anchors
body:
Fixes #14130

The `[#9137]` freeze note in `assertControlledByParentWrite` cited `record-validator.ts:993` (insert mode) and `:1003` (update mode) as the place the three `controlled_by_parent` master-reference shapes are skipped before the required check runs. Both anchors had rotted. This replaces them with a **symbol-relative** citation and adds a standing instruction not to put line numbers back, so the citation cannot rot the same way again.

## Why the anchors mattered, and why swapping the numbers was not the fix

The carrier is a freeze note — the block telling the next author not to widen `omissionRefusedByValidation` for those three shapes. Its authority rests entirely on the reader being able to go and check that `record-validator.ts` really does skip them, and the two anchors were its only evidence pointer. A reader who followed them landed on prose about locale defaults, found no guard, and had to decide whether the note describes code that no longer exists.

The failure mode is specifically the **quiet** one. Re-measured on `origin/main` at `b992b1d64`, not copied from the card:

```
$ git grep -n "if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;" origin/main -- packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts
1037:      if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;
1047:      if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;

$ git show origin/main:packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts | wc -l
1073
```

1073 lines, so `:993` and `:1003` are both **in range**: they resolve, and they resolve to something else — line 993 is `* behavior for any caller that has no principal to read a locale from.` and line 1003 a bare `*` continuation, both inside the `messages?: ValidationMessageContext` docblock. An out-of-range anchor announces itself; one that still resolves does not.

So the repair names the two loop bodies instead of two positions: `validateRecord()` opens the `mode === 'insert'` branch over `Object.entries(fields)` and the `else` update branch over `Object.entries(data)`, each with `if (def.system || def.readonly) continue;`. Substituting `:1037`/`:1047` for `:993`/`:1003` would have repaired this instance and left the class untouched — a few lines added above `record-validator.ts:1037` and the note is wrong again, silently.

`record-validator.ts` itself is **not** touched: it is the referent, not the defect. Nothing in `security-plugin.ts` outside this one freeze note is touched either — the rest of that file stays fenced.

## Clause-2 declaration: `no` on both limbs, with the content limb measured

1. **Path limb — no.** One file, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`. Nothing under `packages/spec/src/**`, no `*.zod.ts` contract schema, no error-code ledger.
2. **Content limb — no, and mechanically confirmed.** Using sibling card #13903's criterion: the changed file was transpiled with `removeComments: true` at the merge base and at this head, and the two emitted outputs are byte-identical.

```
BASE = b992b1d64671296ef9355fc93e23b6efe1e38102
changed files: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts
  packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts: emitted-without-comments bytes 136185 -> 136185; identical=true
VERDICT: NON-COMMENT DIFF EMPTY — comments-only confirmed
```

That green is a measurement rather than a checker that cannot fail — a positive control mutated one executable line in memory (adding braces around the `return` in `if (operation === 'insert' && rel.omissionRefusedByValidation) return;`) and the same comparison went red:

```
control: needle hits=1; emitted bytes 136185 vs 136201; differ=true
CONTROL PASS: the checker does detect a non-comment change
```

Both checker and control ran entirely out of tree (the mutation was a string in memory, never written to the worktree) and are not added to the repo.

## No changeset — `skip-changeset` applied

The diff is comment prose only. It publishes nothing, changes no behaviour, and the byte-identical emit above is the evidence for that rather than an assertion. Writing a changeset here would mean inventing a user-visible change to turn a gate green, so the label is applied instead, as the label exists for exactly this case.

## Verification, all at `737731794`

Gate families derived live at that commit with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, both output sections read whole: 21 path-matched families plus 2 convention-triggered by the i18n-extract config the package owns. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.

- **20 of the 23 derived commands: green.** Including `scripts/check-comment-mask-adoption.mjs`, `scripts/check-keyed-text-bounds.mjs`, `scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs`, `scripts/check-tenant-audit-census.mjs`, `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `check:published-files`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:type-source-resolution`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, and the docs-drift pair.
- **`pnpm check:i18n`: green, after clearing its prerequisite.** It first refused with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built`, which is not a red; the ten-package build closure it names was run under the shared verify lock and the gate then reported `check-i18n-bundles: OK (9 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)`, `plugins/plugin-security  in sync (7 bundle(s))`. `pnpm check:i18n-stale-fill` was green on the first run and needs no build.
- **`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security typecheck`: green** — all three programs, `tsconfig.test.json` included, so the test layer really was type-checked and not excluded.
- **Targeted tests: 4 files, 92 tests passing** — `controlled-by-parent-chain`, `controlled-by-parent-detail-write-authority`, `controlled-by-parent-master-widener`, `controlled-by-parent-sharing`, i.e. the suites that exercise the gate this note governs.

**Two gates are NOT MEASURED locally, declared rather than quietly dropped.** Both exited on an unmet prerequisite before examining anything, and neither can be moved by this diff, since the compiled output they read is byte-identical:

- `node scripts/check-test-completeness.mjs` — exit **3**, which is its own distinct "nothing was measured" code: it wants a saved `turbo run test` log, a CI artifact by construction.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` — exit **3**, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — this gate reads built output`, listing 100+ packages with no `dist/`. Clearing it needs a whole-workspace build; the container's verify lock was already carrying two queued full builds for sibling agents, and CI builds and runs this gate on the PR regardless.

The remaining 79 test files in `plugin-security` were likewise not run, for the same measured reason: with the emitted JavaScript byte-identical, there is no input by which this diff could change a test outcome. CI's `Test Core` shards run them.

## Not in scope here

#13556 (rotted anchors in an ADR pointing into `sql-driver.ts`) is a different carrier and a different site and is untouched by this branch — it remains open. #13722's fence over the rest of `security-plugin.ts` is left standing; this branch does not lift it.
